newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks buttressed by select trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks buttressed by select trade.

text.p: Jordanian stocks were buttressed on Sunday by some select trade in otherwise depressed sentiment over Middle East peace worries, dealers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.07 percent to 147.03 points from 146.93 points on Saturday.
A total of 377,376 shares changed hands in moderate 571,786 dinars volume, with select blue-chip demand buttressing activity.

Brokers said some buying activity with minimal selling pressure recouped some of Saturday's board declines sparked by investors and floor traders pessimism, based on fears of a breakdown in Palestinian-Israeli peace talks.
Industrials led the market with two stock, Livestock and Poultry and El-Zay Ready Wear, focus of some buying interest.
LIPO was focus of investor activity with 216,550 shares changing hands, with the stock rising 0.30 dinar to 0.630 dinar.
Middle East Investment Bank was the sole bank that saw some activity with a slight 0.020 dinar rise to 1.070 dinars. Housing Bank rose a healthy 0.50 dinar to 4.90 dinars in low trade.
The market has remained in a wait-and-see mood since the recent flareup in violence in Palestinian self-rule areas.
Brokers say the market's plight has been worsened by lack of tangible progress in Israeli-Palestinian peace moves to give new impetus to the market, after a recent rebound lost steam.

After gradual gains end of last month that sent the market back above 150 points last week for the first time in four months, shares began to weaken after recent clashes flared in the Israeli occupied West Bank.
Not only the breakdown of Middle East peace talks, but also the delay in implementing a limited oil-for-food deal with Jordan's biggest trading partner Iraq, have hurt trade.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange shed 0.12 percent to 80.63 points, still 15.58 percent down from the same time last year.
A total of 252,788 shares worth 91,351 dinars changed hands in thin trade in the parallel market.
